role: dated access review; not deployment authority
scoreScope: Current live production readiness: development-open policies would permit unauthorized access if treated as production security. This is not a code-quality score.
summary: Git queue reconciled and saved. Kitchen authority and trusted authoring boundaries were checked. Obsolete direct Blog/Product/Price writes were removed from the local candidate. Production deployment remains blocked by open Storage policy and public Product document metadata exposure. No live policy or data changed.

findings.issue: The live named Firestore database and Storage bucket Rules both allow read and write if true. The Firestore policy is the explicitly accepted development policy; neither is production privacy.
findings.recommendation: Keep deployment withheld. Prepare and approve separate Firestore and Storage rollouts with exact target backups and readback; do not silently alter the development policy.

findings.issue: The local candidate permits direct public reads of active public Product roots. Product creation retains internal provisioning state on that root, including actor UID, request ID and recovery fingerprint. Client-side normalizeProduct drops those fields only after the raw document has reached the browser. A local emulator probe returned the internal field unauthenticated.
findings.recommendation: Use a domain-owned safe server projection for public Product collection reads, or move recovery state to a protected child with an explicitly reviewed data transition. Preserve the admin reader and creation retry contract. The existing Product detail API already normalizes its server response.

findings.issue: The prior candidate permitted direct Blog, Product and provider-price writes despite their trusted command owners. This could bypass editorial review, reservation and provider reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Closed locally: direct create/update/delete is now denied, with current command tests and allow/deny regressions. Live permissions remain unchanged.

findings.issue: Place brand/gallery and Ingredient images still have direct client Storage upload consumers. There is no reviewed authored production Storage policy in this repository. Storage Rules cannot consult Kitchen grants in the named misebox database; Firebase supports their Firestore lookups only against the default database.
findings.recommendation: Move membership-protected media writes through the existing trusted server upload mechanics and owning domain authority. Then author/test the bucket policy for the remaining supported direct uploads and public/private reads. Do not add a parallel membership mirror or loosen bucket-wide permissions.
